pages.part: PART 1 - PROBLEM, EXISTING SOLUTIONS, AND VERIFIED GAPS
pages.title: Pathya: a repairable AI textbook reader
items: IMPLEMENTATION-READY PROJECT REPORT | Research cut-off and access date: 16 November 2026

Build Pathya (working name; availability not checked): an accessible web reader that turns a limited set of English and Hindi textbook chapters into navigable, page-linked content. Its core contribution is a trustworthy study workflow: uncertain extraction can be inspected and corrected, and those corrections update narration, search and evidence used by the optional assistant.

A basic OCR + text-to-speech (TTS) reader is a useful baseline but a weak project differentiator. Immersive Reader, Kurzweil 3000, EasyReader, Speechify and NaturalReader already cover substantial reading support; Seeing AI already offers document questions. Source-linked answers also exist in Google's NotebookLM / Gemini Notebook documentation. The opportunity is a focused integration with measurable reliability, not a claim that these components are new. [6-9,13-24,27-28]

Recommended flagships: (1) one structured, page-linked reading model; (2) confidence-aware review with revision-safe corrections; (3) evidence-linked study assistance that abstains when the chapter or its extraction cannot support an answer. Offline chapter reading and user-controlled accessibility settings are essential requirements.
3 students, 14 weeks; approximately 12 focused hours per person per week (504 person-hours). Weeks 15-16 are contingency.
An existing 4-core laptop with 16 GB RAM and 20 GB free space; an Android phone with 4 GB RAM; no dedicated GPU purchase.
School / early college science prose, simple tables and a few teacher-verified equations. English and Hindi first; adults for initial user sessions.
INR 7,000 base cash envelope; up to INR 14,000 with participant and cloud contingencies. Borrowed hardware and student labor excluded.

Part 1 (pp. 1-8) establishes needs, compares 12 solution categories/systems and evaluates evidence. Part 2 (pp. 9-12) defines the product, ranking and evaluation. Part 3 (pp. 13-25) specifies implementation, delivery gates and a numbered bibliography. All numbered citations link to the bibliography; bibliography titles link to original sources.

Evidence labels: V = capability documented by its provider or standard, not independently tested here. R = research result, bounded by its study. I = inference from reviewed evidence. P = proposed implementation. T = proposed target. No software prototype or user study was carried out for this report.

Report quality note: the PDF is designed for readable visual review and includes linked citations and page numbers. It is not certified PDF/UA or claimed to be a fully tagged accessible PDF. The companion HTML carries the same report text, semantic headings and tables for reflow/screen-reader use. Both describe a proposal, not an implemented system.

pages.part: PART 1 - PROBLEM, EXISTING SOLUTIONS, AND VERIFIED GAPS
pages.title: A. Different needs, different study journeys
items: The following are design scenarios, not observations from recruited participants. WAI user stories illustrate why disability labels alone cannot determine an interface. People may have overlapping needs, different screen-reader skills and different preferred languages. Ask about tasks and preferences; do not require a diagnosis to select reader settings. [5]
Blind student: locate an exercise and compare two definitions
An image PDF has no usable text. A flat OCR transcript loses headings, columns, footnotes and the printed page cited by a teacher.
Heading / page / exercise navigation, stable source links, keyboard controls and screen-reader semantics. Audio alone cannot convey a whole page efficiently.
Low-vision student: examine a graph and continue reading
Zooming a fixed page causes repeated panning. Small labels, glare and weak contrast make crops difficult to inspect.
Reflow prose separately from a zoomable source; allow contrast, size and spacing changes, with a clear return point. Preserve magnification and focus.
Student with dyslexia: read, revisit a term and explain a concept
Decoding effort and losing one's place can slow study. Audio may help some tasks; long narration can also overload attention.
Optional sentence highlighting, short playback units, adjustable pace, bookmarks and concise source-linked explanation. Preferences are not treatment.

Poor photographs introduce blur, shadows, skew and clipped lines. Scanned PDFs lack semantic order; even a selectable PDF may have a faulty text layer. Two-column prose, captions and sidebars can interleave. Tables lose header-to-cell relationships when flattened. Equations can lose a minus sign, fraction boundary or exponent while the surrounding paragraph remains fluent. Diagram meaning includes relationships, not just object names. These are engineering risks to test, rather than measured prevalence claims. Document-parsing benchmarks explicitly separate text, tables, formulae and reading order. [33-34]

Multilingual chapters add script changes, English technical terms, abbreviations and numerals. Hindi OCR availability does not guarantee accurate conjuncts, correct language segmentation or intelligible narration. A translated explanation is not the original textbook. Keep source text, pronunciation hints and generated material in separate fields. [6,41,51]
Access is necessary; comprehension is a separate outcome

A student may successfully hear a paragraph yet fail to compare quantities or explain the principle. Test both access tasks (find, read, return, correct) and learning tasks (explain, infer, retrieve supporting evidence). A proposed journey is: import at college Wi-Fi, review flagged content with a teacher, download a chapter, study on the bus, and resume later. If the page is unreadable, request a better capture or authorized accessible edition instead of presenting guessed text as truth.

pages.part: PART 1 - PROBLEM, EXISTING SOLUTIONS, AND VERIFIED GAPS
pages.title: C. What research and standards support
items: Wood et al. report a positive average comprehension effect (d = 0.35; 95% CI 0.14-0.56).
Study designs and learners vary. This does not predict a gain for this app, Hindi content or each student; measure comprehension separately.
Kuster et al. found no speed/accuracy advantage for Dyslexie. A 2026 meta-analysis abstract reports no consistent reliable benefit.
The 2026 full text was not available. Offer preferences; do not claim fonts, color overlays or AI cure / treat dyslexia.
Docling provides reusable structured parsing; OmniDocBench evaluates diverse documents and components.
Developer reports / benchmark scores are not a local textbook result. Pin versions and measure language, layout and degradation strata.
MathML carries structure; MathCAT enables speech/navigation. MathReader reports improved math speech WER on its test.
Math OCR errors can remain mathematically fatal. No reported WER here is transferred to Pathya or Hindi.
ALCE evaluates answer and citation quality separately; generated citations can remain incomplete.
A real citation can still fail to support a claim. Check evidence entailment; add unanswerable questions and abstention.
VizWiz-LF finds plausible generated answers can contain incorrect visual details. DAISY recommends context-appropriate image descriptions.
Not a textbook diagram efficacy study. Do not publish unreviewed inferred relations as source facts.

WCAG 2.2: target AA for the web app; implement semantic structure, meaningful reading order, keyboard operation, visible/unobscured focus, contrast, reflow, language markup and accessible authentication. Avoid drag-only correction. Test target sizing and redundant data entry as applicable. Automated scans alone cannot establish conformance. [1]

EPUB Accessibility 1.1: use its distinction between content accessibility and discoverability metadata when designing exports; do not label an export conformant without checking the complete requirements. DAISY: navigable, synchronized reading is established practice. MathML Core: reviewed snapshot is a Candidate Recommendation, not a final Recommendation; rendering does not certify speech correctness. [2-4]

Image guidance: provide a concise alternative plus a linked longer description when needed. State diagram type, key labels and relationships in the textbook's context. A description should not add invisible facts. In Pathya, descriptions are teacher-authored or explicitly labeled generated drafts until reviewed. [38]

pages.part: PART 1 - PROBLEM, EXISTING SOLUTIONS, AND VERIFIED GAPS
pages.title: D. Seven opportunities, with bounded claims
items: DAISY synchronization and Docling's representation already exist [4,39]. Linking corrections, audio and Q&A at paragraph revisions is an integration opportunity.
MVP foundation. Stable IDs and page geometry are more useful than a custom graph database.
Vendor OCR and reading are common [9-10,17,22]; standardized textbook error triage and derivative invalidation were not found in reviewed product docs.
Flag low-quality extraction; supply accessible review queue. Need a held-out flagging experiment.
Passage citations already exist [28]; ALCE shows citation quality needs evaluation [35].
Jump from answer to source paragraph, then return to answer. Suppress stale evidence after edits.
Several products support downloaded audio or local reading [18,21,23,26]; offline processing and AI are different.
Cache verified chapter content/audio and position. New imports and cloud explanations may wait.
Reading customization is well established [6,13,17,22]. WAI stories show differing interaction needs [5].
Provide independent controls and presets, then preserve individual changes. Do not market presets as treatment.
OCR models and hosted voices list Hindi [41,51]. End-to-end code-switching quality is not established by a language list.
Small, editable term glossary; bilingual listener test. No automatic textbook translation in MVP.
MathML, MathCAT and math speech research are substantial prior art [3,37,43]. Diagram hallucination risk is documented [36].
MVP renders reviewed MathML and simple header tables. Automatic equation parsing / diagram relation exploration is stretch.

The review searched official Microsoft, Google, Bookshare, Dolphin, Kurzweil, Everway/Texthelp, Speechify, NaturalReader and EDRLab documentation; W3C and DAISY standards/guidance; ACL, CVPR, journal publisher, PubMed/PMC and arXiv records; and named public repositories. Searches included OCR, reading order, offline, language support, document Q&A, citation evaluation, dyslexia fonts and accessible mathematics. Access date is 16 November 2026. This is a targeted desktop review, not a systematic review or a hands-on product audit.

The comparison supports choosing a narrow reliability problem. It cannot support “world first,” exhaustive catalog coverage, comparative accessibility rankings or clinical effects. Pages with inconsistent documentation (notably EasyReader PDF input) are recorded as uncertainty. Exact commercial India prices are intentionally left unverified where the reviewed material did not establish a reliable checkout amount.

Show the same extraction error before and after a correction, prove that stale audio and answers are no longer served, and repeat a study task without internet. This makes the technical contribution inspectable. The hypothesis is that these mechanisms reduce silent errors and recovery effort; only the planned evaluation can establish whether students find the combination useful.

pages.part: PART 2 - PROPOSED SOLUTION, DIFFERENTIATION, AND FEASIBILITY
pages.title: A. The product: study a chapter, trust its provenance
items: Value proposition (P): Pathya helps students navigate an authorized chapter, hear or inspect its content in their preferred way, notice extraction problems and return from explanations to the exact supporting passage. It should remain useful when its assistant is unavailable. The name is a working label, not a trademark claim.

Primary: students who use screen readers or magnification, and students who choose TTS / visual reading supports, studying English or Hindi science prose. Keep blindness, low vision and dyslexia as separate evaluation strata. Secondary: teachers or authorized helpers who review extraction and pronunciation. The initial pilot uses consenting adult students; work with minors requires a separate institutional process.

Core tasks are: import; navigate by heading/page/paragraph; read, bookmark and correct; download; and request evidence-linked explanation. Independent controls cover size/spacing, colors, focus, voice, rate and uncertainty interruptions. Preserve preferences without requiring diagnosis. A helper sees authorized blocks, not the student's entire reading history.

A blind student receives a 12-page authorized physics chapter. At college Wi-Fi, they upload it and hear progress messages. Pathya detects two columns and flags a suspicious minus sign. The student can skip to the review queue, listen to the uncertain text, inspect its provenance or ask an authorized helper to review the crop. The helper corrects it using a labeled text form, not drag-and-drop.

After publication of revision 2, the student downloads the chapter, audio and text. On a phone offline, “Go to printed page 38” opens the right section. Table navigation announces the column header with each value. A bookmark saves the paragraph rather than a pixel offset. The assistant is visibly unavailable offline; search and reading continue. After reconnection, an explanation of acceleration cites a specific paragraph, with a link to open and read the evidence.

A low-vision student uses the same content in reflow with adjustable size and an independently zoomable original page. A student with dyslexia chooses short narration segments and sentence focus, turns highlighting off if distracting, and checks an explanation against the original. No preset silently rewrites textbook sentences.

Outside MVP: arbitrary handwriting; handwriting-to-math; general diagram reasoning; chemistry structures; universal table reconstruction; all Indian languages; full DAISY/EPUB import/export certification; diagnosis or treatment; autonomous tutoring; exam proctoring; Braille production; and large-model training. Camera input is a file/capture control with basic quality feedback, not a guaranteed independent capture guide.

A failed parse must still leave a usable status page, a source-download option if authorized and an explicit way to request review. It must not imply that an inaccessible source image has become accessible merely because an upload succeeded.

pages.part: PART 2 - PROPOSED SOLUTION, DIFFERENTIATION, AND FEASIBILITY
pages.title: B-C. Feature ranking and scope selection
items: The scoring below is a planning judgment, not empirical evidence. Scores run 1-5; larger is better. U = user value (30%); F = feasibility in 14 weeks (25%); D = defensible differentiation despite overlap (15%); R = lower technical risk (15%); C = lower recurring cost (15%). Total = 0.30U + 0.25F + 0.15D + 0.15R + 0.15C. Value and feasibility dominate.

Ranking is not the only decision rule. Accessibility controls outrank “differentiators” but are expected functionality. Table narration scores well but depends on verified headers. Evidence-linked answers score lower; retain them as the third flagship because they directly test the study-to-source return path. If time fails, ship passage retrieval first and cut generative responses, preserving the other two flagships.

MVP: a chapter-scoped accessible reader; PDF/photo ingestion on the laptop; page/heading/paragraph IDs; basic quality signals; correction history and invalidation; English-Hindi segmentation with manual overrides; sentence-level audio; simple tables; reviewed equations/figure descriptions; offline chapter package; and optional online evidence-linked explanation. “Reviewed” is a workflow status, not a guarantee of correctness.

Stretch, only after acceptance gates: word-level timing; an additional tested Indian language; automatic equation candidates reviewed before use; simple labeled diagram relationships; structured HTML export; and more robust camera guidance. Future research: calibrated semantic uncertainty, automatic accessible STEM conversion, learning gains over a semester and robust translation of technical educational content.
Hardest assumption: can unreliable extraction be caught affordably?

In weeks 1-2, annotate 24 development pages (12 English, 12 Hindi), including columns, shadows and symbols. Compare Tesseract-only extraction with Docling plus Tesseract. Plot important-error recall against reviewer effort; count minutes spent reviewing each page. If errors remain silent or repair takes over 3 minutes/page on ordinary pages, narrow ingestion to cleaner PDFs and teacher-prepared chapters. Do not add a chatbot to hide a failed extraction pipeline.

pages.part: PART 2 - PROPOSED SOLUTION, DIFFERENTIATION, AND FEASIBILITY
pages.title: D. Evaluation: extraction and grounded answers
items: Use a frozen evaluation manifest and the same source bytes across systems. Split by source chapter, not by adjacent page: 24 development pages and 48 held-out pages, with degradation variants kept in the same split as their clean originals. Report clean native PDF, clean scan and phone-photo results separately, also by English/Hindi. Proposed thresholds below are feasibility gates, not achieved results.

CER = (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / reference characters; WER uses words. Fix Unicode normalization and tokenization; retain meaningful symbols. Report micro-average and per-page median/tail.
Clean prose: CER <=3% English, <=5% Hindi; degraded pages reported separately, no implied pass.
Two reviewers mark blocks and ordered relations. Pairwise order accuracy = correct comparable block pairs / annotated pairs. Also measure omitted blocks and header/footer intrusion.
>=95% pairwise order on clean pages; >=98% prose block coverage.
Label meaning-changing errors (negation, units, missing lines, symbol errors). Report recall, precision, flagged blocks/page and correction minutes/page.
>=90% critical-error recall with <=25% of prose blocks flagged on development gate; validate again held-out.
20 reviewed expressions: exact normalized structure match, symbol errors, and spoken structure judged by a knowledgeable reviewer. Track coverage and unsupported cases.
No unreviewed auto-extracted equation served as trusted; >=90% correct speech on supported reviewed set.
12 simple tables: cell text accuracy, header association accuracy, row/column completeness and answer-to-cell navigation tasks.
>=95% header association on supported simple tables; merged headers explicitly unsupported unless reviewed.
12 figures: two reviewers score label correctness, relations, omissions and invented facts against the page. Student utility scored separately.
Zero invented factual relations in descriptions published as reviewed; report draft errors separately.
30 supported; 10 absent; 10 misleading premises; 10 from ambiguous/damaged content. Score claim-level correctness and support, citation resolution/entailment and false confident answers.
>=95% citation resolution; >=90% supported factual claims; <=5% unsupported factual claims.
Report correct abstentions on 30 unsafe/unsupported questions and unnecessary abstentions on supported ones. Recall@5 uses manually linked evidence blocks.
>=90% appropriate abstention; <=20% unnecessary abstention; evidence Recall@5 >=90%.

Targets may conflict: raising abstention can increase refusal of answerable questions. Publish coverage versus risk and raw denominators, not just one “accuracy.” Raters should see source crops and reference text, be blind to condition where possible and adjudicate disagreements. An LLM judge may assist triage but is not the sole ground-truth authority. [34-36]

pages.part: PART 2 - PROPOSED SOLUTION, DIFFERENTIATION, AND FEASIBILITY
pages.title: D. Evaluation: people, ablations and device costs
items: B0: Tesseract + flat text + sentence TTS, with the same voice and device. B1: full structured reader. B2: B1 without uncertainty cues/review support. B3: evidence retrieval with source links versus generated evidence-linked explanation. Use the same extraction when testing interface ablations, and the same interface when testing parsers. Compare a suitable installed EasyReader/Thorium edition on prepared accessible content and Seeing AI/Lookout on capture tasks where access permits. Record content preparation time; do not compare an already accessible edition against an unprocessed scan without disclosure.
A feasible formative study, not a clinical trial

Aim for 6-9 consenting adult intended users: approximately 2-3 blind, 2-3 low vision and 2-3 with dyslexia, recruited with an accessibility office if feasible. Sample size is a planning assumption. Reimburse time/transport, provide accessible information sheets, allow withdrawal and avoid requiring disclosure beyond what is necessary. Obtain institutional review requirements before recruitment. Use no simulated disability as a substitute for intended-user feedback.

Run 45-60 minute sessions with training and breaks. Counterbalance two equivalent chapter task sets to reduce learning effects. Tasks: locate an exercise; return from a citation; read a table value; notice a seeded uncertain symbol; resume offline; explain a concept and select its supporting passage. Record completion, help required, navigation errors, recoveries, time and comprehension rubric scores. Ask about trust, fatigue and preferences. Report individual and group-stratified observations; small cells do not establish population effects.
At least 80% independent completion of core find/read/return tasks across sessions; report each group and all assistance. No unresolved keyboard trap or inaccessible critical control.

NVDA + Firefox/Chrome on Windows; TalkBack + Chrome on Android. Keyboard-only end-to-end flows; 200% text and 400% zoom/reflow; focus, contrast, language switching and status messages. axe-core adds regression checks [44,54].
On assumed laptop: first usable clean page <=15 s after upload; 10-page chapter <=3 min; cached navigation <300 ms. Online answer p95 <=15 s on measured network. Report cold/warm and failures.
20-page package <=50 MB with chosen image resolution and audio; show exact bytes, model downloads excluded and reported separately. Throttle to 1 Mbps / 300 ms RTT; interrupt download and resume.

After explicit download, restart app with network disabled; read, navigate, search and bookmark chapter. Clear status for unavailable AI, missing audio and storage eviction. No silent online fallback.
Log pages, TTS characters, input/output tokens, retries and per-job costs; hard API budget cap. Crash worker mid-job, retry, edit while offline, then test conflict and stale-cache behavior.

If intended-user recruitment fails, complete expert/manual checks and disclose the limitation. Do not invent a user study or describe technical test success as accessibility validation or improved learning. A future larger study could test retained understanding after a delay; it is beyond this project's evidence claims.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: A. Concrete stack: accessible reader and extraction
items: Affordable default (P): one TypeScript web app and a Python service/worker on a college laptop. Preprocess chapters there; phones consume prepared chapter packages. A local area network can support a demo, but production phone access and service-worker caching require a trusted HTTPS origin. Localhost on a phone refers to that phone, not the laptop.
Frontend: React + TypeScript + Vite; semantic HTML; CSS controls
A single responsive reader; use native controls first. Alternative: vanilla TypeScript reduces framework overhead. PDF.js renders the optional source pane; reflowed HTML is the main reading surface.
React/Vite/TypeScript commonly permissive; confirm exact lockfile licenses. PDF.js Apache-2.0 verified [46]. Device target: Android 4 GB RAM; measure, do not promise minimum compatibility.
Typed request/response schemas; Python document libraries. Alternative: Node API, but avoid splitting business logic across two backends.
FastAPI MIT verified [53]. One 4-core / 16 GB laptop is the planning target; no per-call API cost locally. Pin a compatible environment after the week-1 spike.
PDF/image ingestion: pdfplumber; PDFium renderer; Pillow / OpenCV
Check native text first; extract coordinates with pdfplumber. Rasterize only necessary pages. Alternative: PyMuPDF is convenient but requires an explicit license decision.
pdfplumber MIT verified [47]. Verify pypdfium2/PDFium notices and OpenCV/Pillow licenses in pinned build. CPU-only; bounded page count/resolution.
Low-cost CPU baseline; preserve word boxes/confidence where available. Explicitly configure language; benchmark mixed-script pages.
Tesseract Apache-2.0; language files listed for English/Hindi [40-41]. Model license/version still recorded. No recurring service charge.
Layout / tables: Docling with selected local OCR adapter
Reuse its layout and document representation; map into a small application schema. Alternative: PaddleOCR/PP-Structure after measurement, rather than running both pipelines in production.
Docling code MIT; PaddleOCR code Apache-2.0 [39,42]. Models have separate notices. Local weights must be predownloaded; CPU memory/latency measured early.
Structured model: JSON Schema + SQLite relational tables
Store typed blocks and edges; no separate graph database required. JSON exports allow debugging and offline transport. Alternative: PostgreSQL if shared deployment grows.
Application-owned schema; record dependency licenses. SQLite database and file store on laptop; no managed database fee.

Optional higher-quality configuration: send only selected, consented low-quality pages to Google Document AI Enterprise OCR or its layout parser, then map the response into the same block schema. Both are documented services, not guaranteed improvements for this corpus. Benchmark quality, response geometry, processing region and revision/version first; preserve the local candidate for audit. [49-50]

Do not send every page to several vendors or train a large model from scratch. The budget and schedule favor assembling and evaluating pretrained components. If no GPU is available, batch preparation is acceptable; phone-side document parsing is outside MVP. A hosted API brings recurring page fees, connectivity and data-processing terms; local tools bring setup, model-download and CPU costs.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: A. Concrete stack: speech, retrieval and operations
items: Speech: eSpeak NG sentence files on preparation server; optional installed device voice
CPU, deterministic file generation and local operation. Less natural than neural voices. Optional Azure Speech produces higher-quality candidate audio plus timing events; listener test decides.

eSpeak core GPL-3.0-or-later [45]; package notices/source obligations reviewed before redistribution. Device voice availability and offline behavior vary. Azure per-character terms and voice-specific SSML limits apply [51-52].
Exact sentence start/end from separate clips; highlight current sentence. Word boundaries only when returned by selected engine and mapped reliably.
Do not estimate word timing by equal durations. Cache by text, language, voice and engine version. No alignment-model training required.
Retrieval: SQLite text search + optional multilingual-e5-small embeddings
Keyword lookup plus 384-dimensional local vectors; brute-force cosine is adequate for a small chapter corpus. Alternative: Postgres/pgvector when scale justifies it.
E5 model card MIT, query:/passage: prefixes and input limits [48]. Test Hindi recall; word tokenization may limit lexical search. CPU inference; no embedding API fee.
Answer generation: Gemini API gemini-3.5-flash-lite; optional [60]

Base mode returns extractive evidence cards. Hosted model receives authorized blocks and returns structured claims. Alternative: licensed small local instruct model on better hardware; not a phone default.
Official stable endpoint supports structured output; this is not a grounding guarantee. Recheck availability, tariff, retention and terms at build time. Hard token/cost limits.
Storage/jobs/cache: SQLite + private files + single durable worker
Jobs table with leases/retries; content-hash derived artifacts. Alternative: Redis/RQ or Celery only when concurrency needs justify another service. IndexedDB/Cache Storage for downloaded chapter.
SQLite/file-system backup and locking tested. Browser quotas/eviction vary. Do not introduce an S3/Redis/graph stack just for a small demo.
Authentication / privacy: local single-user mode; hosted sessions if needed
Local demonstration can avoid student accounts. Shared pilot uses secure session cookies, per-document ownership and authorized reviewer roles.
No raw passwords in app code. Verify auth library licenses and deployment region; collect no diagnosis or speech recordings by default.
Testing / monitoring: pytest, Playwright, axe-core; structured logs
Golden documents, correction dependency tests and keyboard/screen-reader checks. Track stage durations, queue failures, bytes and API usage.
axe-core MPL-2.0 [54]; other pinned licenses recorded. No source text or sensitive query bodies in routine logs. Error metrics do not replace user feedback.

Assume a 16 GB preparation laptop and a 4 GB Android client, not a GPU workstation. Cap processing to one page/job at a time and 20-page demo chapters initially. Measure peak RAM, idle/active CPU, model size and package bytes in week 2. These are proposed deployment limits, not measured library minimums. A neural OCR/VLM alternative may exceed them; retain the simpler local route if it does.

There is no unavoidable hosted AI fee in the base reader: preparation and eSpeak speech can be local. Optional hosted OCR, speech, LLM, storage and HTTPS hosting each add charges. Price the exact chosen configuration at build time; service marketing free tiers are not a reliability or budget guarantee. Maintain a dependency/model inventory with license, version, checksum, attribution and redistribution decision.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: B. Architecture: a small pipeline with clear boundaries
items: Figure 1. Proposed system. The graph is a logical content model stored as ordinary database records. Optional cloud enrichment is isolated; prepared chapter reading does not depend on it.

Client: upload/capture, accessible status, settings, navigation, review forms and offline package manager. API: authorization, content limits, job state, version negotiation and signed/private artifact access. Worker: native-text inspection, image preprocessing, OCR/layout adapters, structured conversion, quality rules, speech and indexing. Publisher: validates a revision manifest and atomically makes it current. It never exposes a half-updated mixture.

1. Client uploads PDF/image with language hints. 2. API validates bytes and creates a job. 3. Worker extracts one page at a time and preserves geometry. 4. Typed blocks and links become a candidate revision. 5. Checks create review items; authorized corrections create a new revision. 6. Speech and search artifacts are built for eligible content. 7. Reader requests a versioned chapter manifest. 8. Q&A retrieves only eligible current blocks. 9. Client downloads a complete package and stores local reading state. 10. Deletion revokes access and removes derivatives through a tracked job.

There are two application processes plus a browser, a relational database and private files. Models are reused, not trained. Parser adapters can be replaced without rewriting the reader; the stable block schema protects the interface. Optional online assistance can fail without blocking access to already prepared content. The complexity budget is spent on correction consistency and accessibility, not on microservices.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: B. Data contracts and provenance
items: Use opaque document and block IDs, not text hashes as public identity. IDs remain stable for ordinary edits; splitting/merging creates explicit successor links. Physical PDF index and teacher-visible printed page label are different. Coordinates refer to a normalized top-left page space; retain the affine transform to the original pixels, crop and rotation so highlights remain correct.

Block types: heading, paragraph, list item, table, table cell, equation, figure and caption. Relations: contains, precedes, caption-of, refers-to, header-for and supersedes. A table stores row/column indices, spans, header associations and cell IDs. An equation stores reviewed MathML, original crop and a fallback spoken description. A figure stores source caption, short alternative and extended description with separate origin/review status.
Multipart bytes + title/language/rights note. Returns document_id and job_id (202). Reject excess size/pages before expensive processing.
State: queued, validating, extracting, review_required, building, ready, failed or cancelled; per-page progress and accessible reason.
Current immutable revision, block/page summaries, chapter packages and artifact hashes. Client may request a known revision.
base_revision + allowed operations. Compare-and-swap; conflicting edit returns 409 with accessible reconciliation fields.
document_id, revision, question, optional block scope. Returns evidence IDs, claims, citations, origin label or abstention reason.
Immediately revokes active access, cancels jobs and schedules physical deletion of source/derivatives; returns deletion job receipt.
Generated material has a different identity

Store original text, accepted corrections, teacher commentary and AI explanations separately. Answer records include model/prompt version, evidence block revisions, generated timestamp and a visible “AI explanation” label. Never index a generated explanation as if it were source evidence. A correction is a transcription repair; a teacher's conceptual rewrite belongs in a labeled note, preserving the original wording for audit.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: B. Extraction, checks and correction propagation
items: Validate MIME by bytes, allow only PDF/JPEG/PNG initially, reject password-protected or malformed documents with an accessible message, and cap page count, pixels, CPU time and decompression size. Process in a non-privileged worker with a timeout and no document-triggered external URL fetch. Keep source bytes immutable; store processed crops as derivatives. Strip unnecessary camera metadata from working images. These are proposed controls, not a completed security assessment.

Inspect native text coverage and coordinate plausibility before OCR. A mixed PDF may require OCR only on some pages. For photos, test rotation, deskew, crop and conservative contrast correction; do not erase faint minus signs through aggressive thresholding. Docling gives block/layout candidates; Tesseract eng+hin supplies a transparent baseline. Record all parser/model versions and map coordinates back to the source. [39-41,47]
Checks are layered, not a single confidence number

Check empty/duplicate regions, paragraph coverage, column progression, header repetition, impossible character sequences, suspicious script mixing and orphaned captions. Flag formula/table regions separately. Reserve numeric thresholds for development tuning. Text from native PDFs may have no OCR confidence; label it “not scored,” not “100%.” Randomly review a sample of apparently good blocks to detect silent errors. Keep a visible source and edit trail for every accepted correction.
Figure 2. Correction transaction and rebuild. A published revision is immutable; a newer one replaces it only after required artifacts pass validation.

An accepted edit increments the block and document revision in one transaction, records the operation, and marks dependent speech, chunks, embeddings and answers stale. New read/answer requests resolve the new version; stale derivatives cannot be served under its manifest. Rebuild only affected units. Until audio is ready, show text or synthesize the new sentence; do not play old audio as current. An affected answer remains in history with a stale warning, excluded from current answers.

Reading order edits also invalidate sequence manifests and table/figure adjacency. Re-extraction never silently overwrites teacher corrections: propose a new candidate, match by geometry/text, and request reconciliation when IDs cannot be preserved. Two offline reviewers editing the same base revision cause a conflict rather than last-writer-wins. Keep old references resolvable as historical versions while permission and retention allow.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: B. Narration, offline use and privacy
items: Split paragraphs into language-tagged sentences, with manual overrides for abbreviations and mixed English-Hindi terms. Generate one clip per sentence and store text offsets, clip duration, block revision and voice. This gives reliable sentence-level highlighting without pretending to have word alignment. For optional Azure synthesis, use returned word/bookmark events only for tested voices; support varies across voice families. [51-52]

A pronunciation glossary maps a term + language + scope to spoken alias or supported phoneme instructions. Scope overrides to document/user so “lead” in chemistry need not alter another book. Keep displayed textbook spelling unchanged. Include units, acronyms and common science terms in a small listener-reviewed English/Hindi list. If TTS fails or a device voice is absent, retain accessible text and cached audio, and announce the missing voice.
Offline package, not an implied offline AI system

A chapter manifest names its revision, trusted block text, navigation, table structure, reviewed math/descriptions, optional source thumbnails, audio hashes and byte sizes. The user explicitly downloads it. Store structured text/settings/bookmarks in IndexedDB and immutable audio/assets in Cache Storage. Verify hashes and switch the active manifest atomically only after required files are present. Keep the old package until replacement succeeds.

Support local navigation, simple text search, sentence playback and bookmarks after restart without network. New OCR and online explanations wait. If audio was not downloaded, offer installed speech only after an offline device check; do not promise that all Web Speech voices work offline. Provide storage usage, download progress, delete-download control and clear recovery when browser eviction removes files. Service workers require HTTPS except local development contexts; configure and test deployment before the pilot.
Retain previous complete package; show missing bytes/files and retry. Do not mark the chapter offline-ready prematurely.
Server revision changes while client offline
Read cached revision with date. Queue bookmarks and correction proposals with base revision; synchronize on reconnection and show conflicts.
Continue reading/search; show evidence passages or a clear assistant-unavailable status. No repeated hidden retries.
Announce the unreviewed figure/equation/table and offer caption/review request. A source crop is supplementary, not an accessible substitute.

Default to private documents, owner/reviewer checks on every API and artifact, HTTPS in hosted mode and secret keys only server-side. Store no diagnosis, microphone recording or unnecessary identifiers. For a pilot, propose source/derivative retention until project end plus 30 days, with immediate user-requested revocation and deletion job completion within 7 days; disclose backup expiry separately (e.g. 30 days). These are policy proposals, not legal compliance claims.

Deletion covers originals and all derivatives. Online clients receive a purge request; disconnected devices require local deletion. Disclose shared-device risks and exact data sent to cloud providers. Review institutional, provider, copyright and applicable data requirements before deployment; this report makes no legal compliance claim.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: B. Grounded assistance and bounded STEM handling
items: Index paragraph-sized chunks of about 150-350 tokens, retaining heading context, page/block IDs and revisions; never split a table cell from its headers. For small chapters start with lexical search and add local E5 vectors after measuring recall. E5 expects query: and passage: prefixes exactly as in the model card; its 384-dimensional embeddings suit a small in-memory index. Truncate/chunk within the selected model's input limit. [48]

Filter by owner, document and current eligible revision before ranking. Retrieve a small set (initially top 5) and include neighboring blocks if needed. Unreviewed critical symbols and generated explanations are excluded from trusted evidence. Send only selected excerpts to an optional hosted LLM. The instruction is to explain from supplied evidence, preserve units/negation, identify missing support and return claim-level allowed evidence IDs. Source text is untrusted data; instructions embedded in a book must not change application behavior.

Validate response schema, allowed IDs, revision and quoted spans deterministically. A valid ID is insufficient: evidence may still not entail the claim. Evaluate with human source comparison; optionally add an entailment checker as a second signal. Low retrieval support, contradictory sources, stale content or unresolved critical extraction should trigger an explicit abstention. A prompt alone cannot guarantee groundedness. [35]
Equations, tables and diagrams: explicit support limits

Equations: MVP accepts teacher-verified MathML for a small supported set (fractions, powers and simple algebra). Expose native MathML and test actual NVDA/browser behavior, including numerator/denominator navigation. Use MathCAT through compatible assistive technology, not a custom speech grammar. A crop-to-LaTeX model is stretch; malformed or unverified expressions remain flagged. MathML can encode an incorrectly transcribed formula perfectly. [3,43-44]

Tables: support rectangular tables with a single header row and optional row headers. Render HTML table semantics, announce “row label; column label; value,” and let users move by cell or request a row summary. Treat merged headers, cross-page tables and ambiguous alignment as review cases. A generated verbal summary is additional commentary, not a replacement for exact cells.

Diagrams: retain caption, short alternative and linked extended description. Prefer teacher-reviewed descriptions for the demo. A stretch relation list may expose “battery connects to resistor” with corresponding label IDs, but only after verification. Do not infer trends from unreadable axes or identify missing labels confidently. Test description correctness and student utility separately; fluent visual language can still hallucinate. [36,38]

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: C. Fourteen-week roadmap and cut rules
items: Planning allocation: 504 person-hours across 3 students. Suggested primary ownership: A reader/accessibility, B extraction/content, C API/retrieval/evaluation. Cross-review every interface. Reserve roughly 20% for integration, accessibility repairs and documentation; weeks 15-16 are optional contingency, not hidden MVP scope.
Rights manifest, 24-page development sample; user-task sketches; parser environment spike.
Native text, Tesseract and Docling run on actual laptop; measure RAM/time. Confirm Hindi OCR and font rendering.
Hardest-risk experiment: annotate key errors/order; compare pipelines and review burden.
Decide clean-PDF vs photo scope; publish errors and flagging curves. Narrow scope if ordinary-page repair exceeds 3 min/page.
Versioned JSON schema, page coordinates and API contracts; accessible reader skeleton.
10 fixture pages retain printed/PDF page mapping; keyboard navigation and labeled controls work.
Durable jobs, ingestion caps, text/layout adapter. Depends on schema.
Interrupted job retries idempotently; no duplicate documents/artifacts or hanging progress.
Correction forms, role checks, revision transactions and dependency invalidation.
Seeded edits make audio/index/answer stale; unauthorized and conflicting edits rejected.
Ten mixed-language passages checked by listeners; missing-voice fallback is explicit.
Reflow, heading/page navigation, preferences, simple table semantics.
NVDA keyboard tasks and Android TalkBack smoke test; no critical focus trap.
Offline manifests, cache/download controls and resume.
Airplane-mode restart reads downloaded text/audio; interrupted update keeps valid old package.
Chapter retrieval, evidence cards and citation return navigation.
Development evidence Recall@5 measured; cross-document leakage/stale references rejected.
Optional generated explanations with abstention; reviewed MathML/figures.
Question set includes missing evidence and injected book instructions; enforce ID/revision checks.
Freeze features; complete extraction/Q&A held-out tests and failure drills.
Report all denominators, supported coverage, per-language errors and measured resource costs.
Consent-based formative sessions or disclosed expert fallback.
Document independent task success, assistance, preferences and group-specific barriers.
Fix highest-impact barriers; repeat only affected checks.
No unresolved blocker in upload/read/find/return/offline/delete flows; report remaining limitations.
Release package, reproducible demo, model/license manifest and final report.
Fresh-machine setup verified; demo works without cloud; achieved results clearly separate from targets.
Contingency: repair/integration; selected stretch only after gates.
No new flagship; repeat affected evaluation and freeze final version.
What to cut, and what to protect

Cut in order: automatic diagram relations; automatic equation OCR; word-level alignment; extra languages; generative answer prose. Keep passage retrieval and source links. If extraction is weak, deliver teacher-reviewed chapter preparation and disclose preparation effort. Protect accessible navigation, correction consistency, offline restart and honest status labeling. If only 12 weeks are available, combine weeks 9-10 as extractive evidence support and move feature freeze to week 9; use weeks 10-12 for testing, repairs and release.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: C. Evaluation corpus and costed delivery
items: A small corpus with a rights ledger

Prepare 72 unique pages: 24 development and 48 held-out, from disjoint chapters. Aim for 24 English science pages from the specifically licensed OpenStax Physics edition, 24 Hindi / mixed-language science pages authored by the team or supplied by a teacher with written adaptation/testing permission, and 24 varied supplementary pages split between team-made layouts and clearly licensed StoryWeaver books. StoryWeaver material is a multilingual narrative/illustration stress case, not a science-textbook substitute. Final selection is a week-1 deliverable, not a corpus already acquired. [55-58]

Across this set, select 20 equations, 12 simple tables and 12 figures for separate annotation. Include single/two-column prose, sidebars, footnotes, mixed script and technical units. For 12 source pages create clean scans plus skew/blur/shadow phone variants; keep variants in the same split and report them separately, not as independent originals. Two people check text/order/STEM references; adjudicate disagreements before testing.

Record source URL, title, edition/date, chapter/page, creator, download date, checksum, exact license, third-party asset exclusions, attribution and permission evidence. The reviewed Physics preface says CC BY 4.0, while OpenStax's general current help describes CC BY-NC-SA. Check the exact downloaded edition/file and every selected asset; do not generalize either notice. StoryWeaver books/images use CC BY 4.0 with attribution, while readalongs/videos have different restrictions. Use book assets only. NCERT access does not imply republication permission: its notice prohibits rehosting. Exclude NCERT from the redistributed demo without permission. [55-59]
Budget envelope: planning allocations, not vendor quotations
Participant time / local travel: 6 sessions x 500; up to 9 x 700
Optional APIs: OCR/TTS/LLM combined hard spending cap
Printing / phone data / simple capture stand
Total cash envelope (existing hardware and labor excluded)

The base month-to-month reader can run locally without paid model calls. The allocations above do not promise that any named service costs that amount. Track API cost as pages x OCR rate + TTS characters/1M x speech rate + input tokens/1M x input rate + output tokens/1M x output rate + storage/egress; add retries, taxes and currency conversion when relevant. Use current provider tariffs before enabling a paid route, with user-visible limits and a server-side stop.

Storage sanity check (assumption): 20 pages x 500 words / 150 spoken words per minute is about 66.7 minutes. At 32 kbit/s, compressed audio is about 16 MB (decimal); add thumbnails, text and manifests. This explains the proposed 50 MB package target, not a measured result. Store actual durations and bytes because language, rate and encoding change the total.

pages.part: PART 3 - TECH STACK, ARCHITECTURE, AND BUILD PLAN
pages.title: D. Build first, demonstrate honestly, publish limits
items: Implement one 10-12 page English/Hindi demonstration chapter using the final block schema, accessible heading/page navigation and sentence reading. Then add one text/order correction that atomically invalidates audio and retrieval and rebuilds them. Run that path offline after download. Only once this works should the team add evidence-linked generation. This sequence makes the first usable product independent of LLM availability.
Upload a legally usable chapter; show page count, physical/printed page mapping, extraction progress and declared language scope.
Navigate by heading and printed page with keyboard/NVDA; reflow at large text; toggle narration independently of screen-reader speech.
Open a clearly disclosed seeded OCR/symbol issue. Correct through a labeled form. Show revision increment and stale derivative states.
Listen to rebuilt sentence; read a simple table cell with its row/column headers; inspect one explicitly pre-reviewed equation.
Ask a supported question, open its exact evidence paragraph and return. Ask an unsupported question and receive a meaningful abstention.
Disable network, restart and resume the downloaded chapter; search and bookmark. Show assistant unavailable without blocking reading.
Reconnect and show revision synchronization, then deletion receipt. Present held-out measurements, preparation time and remaining failures.
An honest novelty statement for the project review

“Pathya is a student-built integration of structured textbook extraction, accessible reading and evidence-linked study support. Our proposed contribution is a revision-aware workflow that exposes extraction uncertainty and propagates corrections to narration, navigation and answer evidence, evaluated on a bounded English-Hindi corpus and affordable devices. We do not claim that OCR, TTS, document chat, source citations or accessible math navigation are new.”

Uncertainty heuristics can miss fluent but wrong OCR; human review remains necessary. Hindi technical pronunciation and mixed-script search require native-speaker testing. Reviewed MathML/descriptions restrict scale, and helper dependence may reduce independence. Browser storage can be evicted, online services can change, and a small user sample cannot prove educational or clinical efficacy. The project needs a named maintenance owner after the semester to remain dependable.

Continue only if early experiments establish a useful extraction-and-repair workflow. Success means supported content stays navigable, corrections stay consistent and students can check evidence with manageable effort. Publish failures and unsupported content coverage alongside aggregate scores. No accuracy, learning gain, novelty or cost saving has been measured by this report.
